source.text: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν διήρχετο τὴν Ἰεριχώ.

records.literal_gloss: And having entered he was passing through the Jericho.

en.L: And having entered, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through Jericho.
en.B: Jesus entered Jericho and was making {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way through the town.
en.R: Jesus came to the town of Jericho and was walking through it.

es.L: Y habiendo entrado, atravesaba Jericó.
es.B: Jesús entró en Jericó e iba atravesando la ciudad.
es.R: Jesús llegó al pueblo de Jericó e iba caminando por sus calles.

fr.L: Et, étant entré, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} traversait Jéricho.
fr.B: Jésus entra dans Jéricho et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} traversait la ville.
fr.R: Jésus est arrivé dans la ville de Jéricho. Il marchait à travers la ville.

sw.L: Na akiisha kuingia, alikuwa akipita katikati ya Yeriko.
sw.B: Yesu aliingia Yeriko, akawa anapita katikati ya mji huo.
sw.R: Yesu alifika katika mji wa Yeriko, akawa anatembea katikati ya mji.

vi.L: Và sau khi vào [thành], {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang đi xuyên qua Giê-ri-cô.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu vào Giê-ri-cô và đang đi qua thành ấy.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đến thành Giê-ri-cô và đi ngang qua thành.

ko.L: 그리고 [여리고에] 들어가셔서, 그분이 여리고를 지나가고 계셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 여리고에 들어가셔서 그곳을 지나가고 계셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 여리고라는 마을에 오셔서 그 마을을 걸어서 지나가고 계셨다.

pt.L: E, tendo entrado, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} atravessava Jericó.
pt.B: Jesus entrou em Jericó e estava atravessando a cidade.
pt.R: Jesus chegou à cidade de Jericó e ia passando por ela.

decisions.choice: Jericho: a town in the Jordan valley, on the road up to Jerusalem
alternatives: the ancient ruined city of Joshua's time
decisions.reason: Jericho lay about fifteen miles northeast of Jerusalem and some three thousand feet lower. Pilgrims from Galilee who came down the Jordan valley went up to Jerusalem from there (10:30; 18:35). It was a rich town, with a customs post on a main route, which explains a chief tax collector living there.

decisions.choice: was passing through: the action under way when the next event happens
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense shows Jesus in the middle of crossing the town. He meant to go on, which makes his stopping at Zacchaeus' house in 19:5 the more striking.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives; none here (atravesaba)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb, so there is nothing separate to capitalise. The setting therefore covers fewer words than in English, as in Matthew. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal
decisions.reason: As in John, Mark and Luke 2 and 4: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, and the parable of 19:12-27 is in the passé composé (see 19:12). This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on verb prefixes (alikuwa akipita)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb's prefix, which cannot take a capital, so spans go only on free pronouns and possessives, as in Matthew and John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English through the chapter.

decisions.choice: The narrator calls Jesus "Ngài"; Jesus says "Ta" of himself; the verb for his speaking is "nói" (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The settled forms of the Vietnamese style guide (sections 6 and Settled), as in the rest of Luke.

decisions.choice: "Giê-ri-cô"
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of the name, as in Luke 10:30.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through Luke 19-21; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Literal refers to him as "그분", Jesus speaks in 해라체 and people speak to him in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (Korean style guide, sections 4 and 7).

decisions.choice: "여리고" at every level
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of the name, as in the Korean Luke 10:30 and Mark 10:46.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι καλούμενος Ζακχαῖος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀρχιτελώνης καὶ αὐτὸς πλούσιος·

records.literal_gloss: And look, a man by name being called Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector and he [was] rich;

en.L: And look, [there was] a man called by the name Zacchaeus; and he was a chief tax collector, and he [was] rich.
en.B: A man named Zacchaeus lived there. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
en.R: A man named Zacchaeus lived there. He was the head of the tax collectors in that area, and he was very rich.

es.L: Y mira, [había] un hombre llamado por nombre Zaqueo; y él era jefe de publicanos, y él [era] rico.
es.B: Allí vivía un hombre llamado Zaqueo. Era jefe de los cobradores de impuestos, y era rico.
es.R: Allí vivía un hombre llamado Zaqueo. Era el jefe de los cobradores de impuestos de esa zona, y era muy rico.

fr.L: Et voici, [il y avait] un homme appelé du nom de Zachée ; et il était chef des collecteurs d’impôts, et il [était] riche.
fr.B: Là vivait un homme nommé Zachée. C’était un chef des collecteurs d’impôts, et il était riche.
fr.R: Un homme qui s’appelait Zachée habitait là. Il était le chef des collecteurs d’impôts de la région, et il était très riche.

sw.L: Na tazama, [palikuwa na] mtu aitwaye kwa jina Zakayo; naye alikuwa mkuu wa watoza ushuru, naye [alikuwa] tajiri.
sw.B: Huko kulikuwa na mtu mmoja jina lake Zakayo. Alikuwa mkuu wa watoza ushuru, tena alikuwa tajiri.
sw.R: Huko aliishi mtu mmoja aitwaye Zakayo. Alikuwa mkubwa wa watoza ushuru wote wa eneo hilo, naye alikuwa tajiri sana.

vi.L: Và kìa, [có] một người tên gọi là Xa-chê; ông là trưởng ban thu thuế, và ông giàu có.
vi.B: Ở đó có một người tên là Xa-chê. Ông là trưởng ban thu thuế, và là người giàu có.
vi.R: Ở đó có một người tên là Xa-chê. Ông đứng đầu những người thu thuế trong vùng ấy, và ông rất giàu.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 이름이 삭개오라고 불리는 사람이 [있었다]. 그는 세리장이었고 그는 부자였다.
ko.B: 그곳에 삭개오라는 사람이 있었다. 그는 세리장이었고 부자였다.
ko.R: 그곳에 삭개오라는 사람이 살고 있었다. 그는 그 지역에서 세금 걷는 사람들의 우두머리였고, 큰 부자였다.

pt.L: E eis que [havia] um homem chamado pelo nome de Zaqueu; e ele era chefe dos cobradores de impostos, e ele [era] rico.
pt.B: Morava ali um homem chamado Zaqueu. Ele era chefe dos cobradores de impostos e era rico.
pt.R: Morava ali um homem chamado Zaqueu. Ele era o chefe dos cobradores de impostos daquela região e era muito rico.

decisions.choice: chief tax collector: a man in charge of collecting tolls and taxes in a district, with other collectors working under him
alternatives: a high official of the Roman government
decisions.reason: The word is found nowhere else in Greek writing before Luke, and is built from "chief" and "tax collector". Collectors bid for the right to gather the tolls of an area and kept what they took above the agreed sum (3:12-13). A chief collector probably held the contract and had others collect for him, so he grew rich from their work as well as his own. Tax collectors were despised as cheats and as servants of foreign rulers (5:30; 18:10-13).

decisions.choice: rich: Luke sets this rich man beside the rich ruler of 18:18-25
decisions.reason: Jesus has just said that it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom of God, but that what is impossible for people is possible for God (18:24-27). Zacchaeus is a rich man who is saved (19:9).

decisions.choice: Zacchaeus: a Jewish name
decisions.reason: The name is a Greek form of a Hebrew name meaning "clean" or "innocent" (Ezra 2:9 has a family of that name). He is a Jew, a son of Abraham (19:9), working in a trade his people despised.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: lived there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the man was, as "look" points to someone the reader meets in Jericho.

decisions.choice: the head of the tax collectors in that area
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title (m1).

decisions.choice: jefe de publicanos (L); jefe de los cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used through the Gospels: "publicanos" at Literal, the traditional word, and the plain "cobradores de impuestos" at Balanced and Readable, which a reader today understands. Zacchaeus was over the other collectors of the district (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mira (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-1): Literal keeps the Greek pointer word; Balanced and Readable introduce Zacchaeus with "Allí vivía", which does the same work.

decisions.choice: chef des collecteurs d’impôts at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet (style guide 9) says "collecteurs d’impôts" in every book; "publicain" is a church word that most readers no longer understand. Readable adds "de la région", as the English Readable explains the title (m1).

decisions.choice: voici (L); not rendered as a separate word (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 2:10: French "voici" is still the ordinary word for pointing to someone new, so Literal keeps it where English Literal says "look".

decisions.choice: mkuu wa watoza ushuru (L, B); mkubwa wa watoza ushuru wote wa eneo hilo (R)
decisions.reason: "Watoza ushuru" is the term used through the Gospels. Zacchaeus was over the other collectors of the district (meaning decision m1); Readable says so, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Xa-chê"; "trưởng ban thu thuế" (L, B); "đứng đầu những người thu thuế trong vùng ấy" (R)
alternatives: người đứng đầu bọn thu thuế
decisions.reason: "Xa-chê" is the Protestant form of the name. "trưởng ban thu thuế" names a man in charge of other collectors (meaning decision) in a neutral word; the older "bọn" sounds contemptuous in the narrator's mouth. Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: "kìa" (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps "look"; Balanced and Readable let the new scene speak for itself.

decisions.choice: "보라" (L) for idou, through Luke 19-21; not rendered as a word (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 9:30, 11:31 and 13:7; Balanced and Readable leave the attention-getter unsaid, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "삭개오"; "세리장" (L, B), "세금 걷는 사람들의 우두머리" (R)
decisions.reason: The Protestant form of the name; "세리장" is the short word for a chief tax collector, built on "세리" as in Luke 5:27, and Readable spells it out as it does "세리".

source.text: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τίς ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ὅτι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ μικρὸς ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: and he was seeking to see the Jesus who he is, and not he was able because of the crowd, because in the stature small he was.

en.L: And he was trying to see who Jesus was, and he was not able to because of the crowd, for he was small in stature.
en.B: He was trying to see who Jesus was, but he could not see over the crowd, because he was a short man.
en.R: He wanted to see what Jesus was like. But there were too many people, and Zacchaeus was too short to see over them.

es.L: Y procuraba ver a Jesús, quién era, y no podía a causa de la multitud, porque era pequeño de estatura.
es.B: Quería ver quién era Jesús, pero la multitud se lo impedía, porque era de baja estatura.
es.R: Quería ver cómo era Jesús. Pero había demasiada gente, y Zaqueo era tan bajito que no podía ver por encima de ellos.

fr.L: Et il cherchait à voir qui était Jésus, et il ne [le] pouvait pas à cause de la foule, car il était petit de taille.
fr.B: Il cherchait à voir qui était Jésus, mais il n’y arrivait pas à cause de la foule, car il était de petite taille.
fr.R: Il voulait voir à quoi ressemblait Jésus. Mais il y avait trop de monde, et Zachée était trop petit pour voir par-dessus les gens.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akitafuta kumwona Yesu ni nani, wala hakuweza kwa sababu ya umati, kwa kuwa alikuwa mfupi wa kimo.
sw.B: Alitaka sana kumwona Yesu ni nani, lakini hakuweza kuona kwa sababu ya umati wa watu, kwa kuwa alikuwa mtu mfupi.
sw.R: Alitaka kumwona Yesu jinsi alivyo. Lakini watu walikuwa wengi mno, na Zakayo alikuwa mfupi sana, hakuweza kuona juu yao.

vi.L: Và ông tìm cách xem Đức Giê-xu là người thế nào, nhưng không thể được vì đám đông, vì ông thấp người.
vi.B: Ông muốn xem thử Đức Giê-xu là ai, nhưng không thấy được vì đám đông, bởi ông thấp người.
vi.R: Ông muốn nhìn xem Đức Giê-xu là người thế nào. Nhưng người ta đông quá, và Xa-chê lại thấp, nên ông không nhìn qua đầu họ được.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 예수께서 어떤 분이신지 보려고 애쓰고 있었으나, 무리 때문에 볼 수 없었다. 그가 키가 작았기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그는 예수께서 어떤 분이신지 보려고 애썼지만, 키가 작아서 무리에 가려 볼 수가 없었다.
ko.R: 삭개오는 예수께서 어떤 분이신지 보고 싶었다. 그러나 사람들이 너무 많았고, 삭개오는 키가 작아서 사람들 너머로 볼 수가 없었다.

pt.L: E ele procurava ver quem era Jesus, e não conseguia por causa da multidão, pois era pequeno de estatura.
pt.B: Ele estava tentando ver quem era Jesus, mas não conseguia por causa da multidão, porque era um homem baixo.
pt.R: Ele queria ver como Jesus era. Mas havia gente demais, e Zaqueu era baixo demais para enxergar por cima das pessoas.

decisions.choice: small in stature: short
decisions.reason: The noun can mean age or height. Here, where he cannot see over a crowd and climbs a tree, it means height.

decisions.choice: he was small: Zacchaeus, not Jesus
decisions.reason: Grammatically "he" could refer to either man. But the one who runs ahead and climbs a tree to see is Zacchaeus, so he is the short one.

decisions.choice: trying to see who Jesus was: wanting to see this man for himself
decisions.reason: The verb "seek" is used again in 19:10, where the Son of Man comes to seek the lost. Zacchaeus is looking for Jesus, but Jesus is the one who finds him.

decisions.choice: too short to see over them; Zacchaeus
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain how his height stopped him seeing and names the short man (m2).

decisions.choice: "예수께서 어떤 분이신지" for "who Jesus was"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the clause as wanting to see this man for himself; "어떤 분이신지" says that more naturally than "누구이신지", which would sound like asking for his name.

source.text: καὶ προδραμὼν εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ συκομορέαν ἵνα ἴδῃ αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐκείνης ἤμελλεν διέρχεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having run ahead to the front he went up onto a sycamore-fig tree in order that he might see him, because that [way] he was about to pass through.

en.L: And running ahead to the front, he climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree so that he might see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was about to pass through that [way].
en.B: So he ran on ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since Jesus was going to come along that road.
en.R: So he ran on ahead of the crowd and climbed up into a fig tree to see Jesus. Jesus was going to pass that way.

es.L: Y corriendo adelante, hacia el frente, subió a un sicómoro para verlo, porque por aquel [camino] iba a pasar.
es.B: Así que corrió adelante y se subió a un sicómoro para verlo, porque Jesús iba a pasar por ese camino.
es.R: Entonces corrió por delante de la gente y se subió a una higuera para ver a Jesús. Jesús iba a pasar por allí.

fr.L: Et, courant en avant, il monta sur un sycomore afin de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait passer par là.
fr.B: Il courut donc en avant et grimpa sur un sycomore pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir, car Jésus devait passer par ce chemin.
fr.R: Alors il a couru devant la foule et il est monté dans un figuier pour voir Jésus. Jésus allait passer par là.

sw.L: Basi akatangulia mbio mbele, akapanda juu ya mkuyu ili amwone, kwa sababu alikuwa karibu kupita [njia] ile.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo alikimbia mbele, akapanda mkuyu ili amwone, kwa sababu Yesu angepita njia hiyo.
sw.R: Basi alikimbia mbele ya umati, akapanda juu ya mti wa mkuyu ili amwone Yesu. Yesu alikuwa karibu kupita njia hiyo.

vi.L: Và chạy trước lên phía trước, ông trèo lên một cây sung để thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp đi qua lối đó.
vi.B: Vậy ông chạy lên trước, trèo lên một cây sung để xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì Đức Giê-xu sắp đi qua đường ấy.
vi.R: Vì thế ông chạy lên trước đám đông và trèo lên một cây sung để nhìn thấy Đức Giê-xu. Đức Giê-xu sắp đi qua lối ấy.

ko.L: 그래서 그는 앞으로 달려가서, 그분을 보려고 돌무화과나무에 올라갔다. 그분이 그 [길로] 지나가시려 했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그래서 그는 앞으로 달려가 돌무화과나무에 올라갔다. 예수를 보려는 것이었다. 예수께서 그 길로 지나가실 참이었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 삭개오는 사람들보다 앞서 달려가서 무화과나무에 올라갔다. 예수를 보려는 것이었다. 예수께서 그 길로 지나가실 참이었다.

pt.L: E, correndo adiante, para a frente, ele subiu num sicômoro para vê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava para passar por aquele [caminho].
pt.B: Então ele correu na frente e subiu num sicômoro para vê-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}, pois Jesus ia passar por aquele caminho.
pt.R: Então ele correu na frente da multidão e subiu numa figueira para ver Jesus. Jesus ia passar por ali.

decisions.choice: sycamore-fig: a kind of fig tree with a short trunk and wide, low branches
alternatives: the sycamore or plane tree of northern countries
decisions.reason: This tree grew in the warm lowlands such as the Jordan valley (1 Kings 10:27; Amos 7:14). Its short trunk and spreading low branches made it easy to climb. It is not the tree called sycamore in Europe or North America.

decisions.choice: running ahead: a rich man setting aside his dignity
decisions.reason: Grown men of standing did not run in public or climb trees. Zacchaeus does both to see Jesus.

decisions.choice: that way: along that road
decisions.reason: The word is a pronoun meaning "that one", with "way" or "road" understood.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus so that the reader can tell the two men apart.

decisions.choice: fig tree
decisions.reason: Readable keeps it simple; the tree was a kind of fig (m1). Literal and Balanced give its full name.

decisions.choice: sicómoro (L, B); higuera (R)
decisions.reason: The tree is the sycamore-fig, a fig tree with low, wide branches (meaning decision m1); "sicómoro" is its Spanish name. Readable says simply "higuera" (fig tree), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: un sycomore (L, B); un figuier (R)
decisions.reason: French "sycomore" is the usual name of this fig tree of the Near East (m1), so Literal and Balanced need no compound like the English "sycamore-fig". Readable says "un figuier", as the English Readable says "fig tree", because many French readers know "sycomore" as a kind of maple.

decisions.choice: mkuyu at every level
decisions.reason: The tree is the sycamore-fig (meaning decision m1), which Swahili calls "mkuyu"; it is a familiar tree in East Africa, so Readable keeps the name where the English Readable says "fig tree".

decisions.choice: "cây sung" at every level
decisions.reason: The sycamore-fig is a fig with low, wide branches (meaning decision). "cây sung", the cluster fig Vietnamese readers know, is its near relative and the familiar Protestant word here; "cây vả" is kept for the common fig (Luke 13:6; 21:29).

decisions.choice: "돌무화과나무" (L, B); "무화과나무" (R) for sykomorea
decisions.reason: The tree is a kind of fig (meaning decision). The older Korean Bibles' "뽕나무" (mulberry) names a different tree; Readable keeps the plain "fig tree", as the English does.

decisions.choice: [길로]
decisions.reason: Greek "that [way]" leaves the noun unsaid; Korean needs it.

decisions.choice: sicômoro (L, B); uma figueira (R)
decisions.reason: Unlike English "sycamore", Portuguese "sicômoro" is the name of this very tree, the fig of the Jordan valley (m1), so Literal and Balanced need no compound. Readable says "figueira", as the English Readable says "fig tree".

source.text: καὶ ὡς ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον, ἀναβλέψας ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζακχαῖε, σπεύσας κατάβηθι, σήμερον γὰρ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου δεῖ με μεῖναι.

records.literal_gloss: And when he came to the place, having looked up the Jesus said to him, Zacchaeus, having hurried come down, today for in the house of you it is necessary [for] me to stay.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to the place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry [and] come down, for today I must stay at your house."
en.B: When Jesus reached the spot, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hurry down. Today is the day I have to stay in your home."
en.R: When Jesus came to that place, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up at Zacchaeus. He said, "Zacchaeus, come down from there, and be quick! Today I need to stay at your house."

es.L: Y cuando llegó al lugar, Jesús, alzando la vista, le dijo: «Zaqueo, date prisa [y] baja, porque hoy es necesario que yo me quede en tu casa».
es.B: Cuando Jesús llegó a aquel sitio, alzó la vista y le dijo: «Zaqueo, baja enseguida. Hoy es el día en que tengo que quedarme en tu casa».
es.R: Cuando Jesús llegó a ese lugar, miró hacia arriba, a Zaqueo, y le dijo: «¡Zaqueo, baja de ahí, y rápido! Hoy necesito quedarme en tu casa».

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arriva à l’endroit, Jésus, levant les yeux, lui dit : « Zachée, dépêche-toi de descendre, car aujourd’hui il faut que je reste dans ta maison. »
fr.B: Quand Jésus arriva à cet endroit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leva les yeux et lui dit : « Zachée, descends vite. C’est aujourd’hui que je dois loger chez toi. »
fr.R: Quand Jésus est arrivé à cet endroit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a levé les yeux vers Zachée. Il lui a dit : « Zachée, descends de là, et vite ! Aujourd’hui, je dois rester dans ta maison. »

sw.L: Na alipofika mahali pale, Yesu alitazama juu akamwambia, "Zakayo, fanya haraka ushuke, kwa maana leo imenipasa kukaa nyumbani mwako."
sw.B: Yesu alipofika mahali hapo, alitazama juu, akamwambia, "Zakayo, shuka upesi. Leo ndiyo siku ambayo lazima nikae nyumbani kwako."
sw.R: Yesu alipofika mahali hapo, alimtazama Zakayo juu. Akamwambia, "Zakayo, shuka kutoka huko juu, tena haraka! Leo ninahitaji kukaa nyumbani kwako."

vi.L: Và khi đến chỗ ấy, Đức Giê-xu nhìn lên và nói với ông: "Xa-chê, hãy mau xuống, vì hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phải ở lại nhà ông."
vi.B: Khi đến chỗ ấy, Đức Giê-xu nhìn lên và nói với ông: "Xa-chê, hãy mau xuống đi! Hôm nay chính là ngày {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phải ở lại nhà ông."
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu đến chỗ đó, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhìn lên Xa-chê. Ngài nói: "Xa-chê, hãy xuống đây, nhanh lên! Hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cần ở lại nhà ông."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그곳에 이르셨을 때에, 예수께서 쳐다보시고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "삭개오야, 서둘러 내려오너라. 오늘 내가 네 집에 머물러야 하겠기 때문이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그곳에 이르러 위를 쳐다보시고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "삭개오야, 어서 내려오너라. 오늘은 내가 꼭 네 집에 머물러야 하겠다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그곳에 오셔서 삭개오를 올려다보셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "삭개오야, 빨리 내려오너라! 오늘은 내가 네 집에 묵어야 한다."

pt.L: E, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chegou ao lugar, Jesus olhou para cima e lhe disse: "Zaqueu, apresse-se [e] desça, pois hoje é necessário que eu fique na sua casa."
pt.B: Quando Jesus chegou àquele lugar, olhou para cima e lhe disse: "Zaqueu, desça depressa. Hoje é o dia em que eu preciso ficar na sua casa."
pt.R: Quando Jesus chegou ali, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} olhou para cima, para Zaqueu, e disse: "Zaqueu, desça daí, e depressa! Hoje eu preciso ficar na sua casa."

decisions.choice: must: it is God's will that Jesus stay there
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for what God has planned and Jesus must carry out (2:49; 4:43; 9:22; 13:33). Staying with a tax collector is part of the work Jesus was sent to do (19:10).

decisions.choice: today: salvation comes now
alternatives: only the date of the visit
decisions.reason: "Today" comes again in 19:9: today salvation has come to this house. Luke uses the word for the moment God's salvation arrives (2:11; 4:21; 23:43).

decisions.choice: stay at your house: be his guest, sharing food and perhaps lodging
decisions.reason: To stay in someone's house and eat with him was to accept him. Jesus invites himself, and does it publicly.

decisions.choice: the place: the tree where Zacchaeus was
alternatives: a known place in the town
decisions.reason: The place is the spot on the road beside the tree he had climbed (19:4).

decisions.choice: Today is the day I have to stay
alternatives: I must stay at your house today
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "today" first, for emphasis (m2). Balanced keeps the stress at the start.

decisions.choice: rester (L, R); loger chez toi (B)
decisions.reason: Here the verb has its ordinary sense of staying as a guest (m3). The style guide keeps "demeurer" for the theological sense; "rester" and "loger" are the everyday words. Balanced's "C’est aujourd’hui que" keeps "today" stressed, as the English Balanced does (m2).

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to Zacchaeus as "ông" (19:5, 19:9)
decisions.reason: The respectful form for a grown man of standing, as Jesus speaks to the scribe in Mark 12:34; the welcome is warm, not condescending.

decisions.choice: "머물러야 하겠다" (L, B); "묵어야 한다" (R) for "I must stay"
decisions.reason: "-야 하다" keeps the sense of necessity that the meaning decision reads as God's will; "머무르다" is the Korean John's word for meno, and Readable uses the everyday word for staying as a guest.

decisions.choice: "삭개오야": Jesus calls him by name in 해라체
decisions.reason: As Jesus addresses Martha (Luke 10:41, "마르다야").

decisions.choice: você (desça, sua casa)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to a man, so he uses "você", the address between people (style §4); the imperatives are in the "você" form ("desça", "apresse-se").

source.text: καὶ σπεύσας κατέβη, καὶ ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν χαίρων.

records.literal_gloss: And having hurried he came down, and he welcomed him rejoicing.

en.L: And hurrying, he came down, and he welcomed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, rejoicing.
en.B: So he hurried down and gladly welcomed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: So Zacchaeus quickly climbed down. He was very happy to welcome Jesus into his home.

es.L: Y dándose prisa, bajó, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibió gozoso.
es.B: Él bajó a toda prisa y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibió con alegría.
es.R: Zaqueo bajó rápidamente. Estaba muy contento de recibir a Jesús en su casa.

fr.L: Et, se dépêchant, il descendit, et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accueillit en se réjouissant.
fr.B: Il descendit en hâte et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accueillit avec joie.
fr.R: Alors Zachée est vite descendu. Il était très heureux d’accueillir Jésus dans sa maison.

sw.L: Naye akafanya haraka, akashuka, akamkaribisha akifurahi.
sw.B: Basi alishuka upesi, akamkaribisha kwa furaha.
sw.R: Zakayo akashuka haraka. Alifurahi sana kumkaribisha Yesu nyumbani kwake.

vi.L: Và ông vội vàng xuống, và vui mừng tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ông liền vội vàng xuống và vui mừng tiếp đón {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Xa-chê vội vàng trèo xuống. Ông rất vui được đón Đức Giê-xu vào nhà mình.

ko.L: 그러자 그가 서둘러 내려와서, 기뻐하며 그분을 맞아들였다.
ko.B: 삭개오는 서둘러 내려와서 기쁘게 예수를 맞아들였다.
ko.R: 삭개오는 얼른 내려왔다. 그리고 아주 기뻐하며 예수를 자기 집으로 모셨다.

pt.L: E, apressando-se, ele desceu e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} recebeu, alegrando-se.
pt.B: Ele desceu depressa e {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} recebeu com alegria.
pt.R: Então Zaqueu desceu depressa. Ele ficou muito feliz de receber Jesus na sua casa.

decisions.choice: welcomed: received as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb is used of receiving someone into one's home (10:38; Acts 17:7).

decisions.choice: rejoicing: the joy of those who receive salvation
decisions.reason: Luke often tells of joy when God's salvation comes (1:14; 2:10; 15:5-7, 32). Zacchaeus' gladness is the first sign of what 19:9 announces.

decisions.choice: into his home
decisions.reason: Readable says where he welcomed Jesus (m1).

decisions.choice: "모셨다" (R) for welcoming Jesus as a guest
decisions.reason: The honorific verb for receiving a respected guest into one's home, matching "into his home" in the English Readable.

source.text: καὶ ἰδόντες πάντες διεγόγγυζον λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἀνδρὶ εἰσῆλθεν καταλῦσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen all were grumbling saying that With a sinful man he has gone in to lodge.

en.L: And seeing [it], all were grumbling, saying, "With a sinful man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has gone in to lodge!"
en.B: Everyone who saw it began to mutter and complain. "He has gone to be a guest at the house of a sinner!" they said.
en.R: Everyone saw this and began to grumble. They said, "He has gone to stay at the home of a man who is a sinner!"

es.L: Y viendo [esto], todos murmuraban, diciendo: «¡Con un hombre pecador ha entrado a hospedarse!».
es.B: Todos los que lo vieron se pusieron a murmurar y a quejarse. «¡Ha ido a alojarse en casa de un pecador!», decían.
es.R: Todos vieron esto y empezaron a quejarse. Decían: «¡Ha ido a quedarse en la casa de un hombre que es pecador!».

fr.L: Et, voyant [cela], tous murmuraient, disant : « C’est chez un homme pécheur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est entré loger ! »
fr.B: Tous ceux qui virent cela se mirent à murmurer et à se plaindre. « Il est allé loger chez un pécheur ! » disaient-ils.
fr.R: Tout le monde a vu cela, et les gens ont commencé à se plaindre. Ils disaient : « Il est allé loger chez un homme qui est un pécheur ! »

sw.L: Na walipoona, wote walikuwa wakinung'unika, wakisema, "Kwa mtu mwenye dhambi ameingia kufikia!"
sw.B: Kila mtu aliyeona jambo hilo alianza kunung'unika na kulalamika. "Amekwenda kuwa mgeni nyumbani kwa mtu mwenye dhambi!" wakasema.
sw.R: Watu wote waliona hayo, wakaanza kunung'unika. Wakasema, "Amekwenda kukaa nyumbani kwa mtu mwenye dhambi!"

vi.L: Và thấy [vậy], mọi người đều lằm bằm, nói rằng: "Ông ta đã vào ở trọ nhà một người tội lỗi!"
vi.B: Ai thấy cũng lằm bằm: "Ông ta lại vào làm khách nhà một người tội lỗi!"
vi.R: Mọi người thấy vậy và bắt đầu phàn nàn. Họ nói: "Ông ta đã đến ở nhà một người tội lỗi!"

ko.L: 그리고 [그것을] 본 모든 사람이 투덜거리며 말했다. "그가 죄인인 사람의 집에 묵으러 들어갔다!"
ko.B: 그것을 본 사람들이 모두 수군거리며 불평했다. "저 사람이 죄인의 집에 손님으로 들어가다니!"
ko.R: 사람들이 모두 이것을 보고 투덜거렸다. 그들이 말했다. "저 사람이 죄인으로 소문난 사람의 집에 묵으러 들어갔다!"

pt.L: E, vendo [isso], todos murmuravam, dizendo: "Com um homem pecador {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi se hospedar!"
pt.B: Todos os que viram aquilo começaram a murmurar e reclamar: "Ele foi se hospedar na casa de um pecador!", diziam.
pt.R: Todos viram isso e começaram a reclamar. Eles diziam: "Ele foi ficar na casa de um homem que é pecador!"

decisions.choice: were grumbling: complaining among themselves
decisions.reason: The same strong form of the verb is used when Pharisees and scribes complain that Jesus welcomes sinners and eats with them (15:2; compare 5:30). Here "all" grumble, not only the leaders.

decisions.choice: a sinful man: a man known for his sin, here because of his trade
alternatives: a man with a hidden sin
decisions.reason: Tax collectors were counted as sinners because they cheated people and worked for foreign rulers (3:12-13; 5:30; 7:34). A guest shared in his host's standing.

decisions.choice: lodge: stay as a guest
decisions.reason: The verb means to break a journey and find lodging (9:12).

decisions.choice: they said, after the quoted words
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the quotation first and gives the speakers after it.

decisions.choice: He has gone ... (no deity_pronoun setting at the start of the quoted sentence)
decisions.reason: The pronoun means Jesus, but it begins a sentence, so it is capitalized either way.

decisions.choice: C’est chez un homme pécheur qu’il est entré loger (L), with the deity_pronoun setting on "il"; Il, capitalised either way (B, R)
alternatives: Chez un homme pécheur il est entré loger, with no span
decisions.reason: English Literal keeps the Greek order, which puts the pronoun after the opening words without a span. French Literal keeps the stress on "chez un homme pécheur" with "C’est ... que", which puts the pronoun for Jesus inside the sentence, so it carries the setting. In Balanced and Readable it begins the quoted sentence and is capitalised either way.

decisions.choice: kufikia
decisions.reason: "Kufikia" is to lodge with someone as a guest (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say it more plainly with "kuwa mgeni" and "kukaa".

decisions.choice: "Ông ta" for Jesus in the grumblers' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The style guide has critics speak of Jesus as "ông ta"; it is a word of the speakers' attitude, not a pronoun the reader's setting should capitalise.

decisions.choice: "nói rằng" (L); the quotation introduced by a colon (B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese introduces the quoted words with a colon where the English Balanced puts "they said" after them.

decisions.choice: The grumblers speak of Jesus with no honorific ("그가", "저 사람이", "들어갔다")
decisions.reason: As the critics in the Korean Luke 15:2 and 7:39: the complaint is said with disapproval.

decisions.choice: "투덜거리다" (L, R), "수군거리며 불평하다" (B); "죄인인 사람" (L), "죄인" (B), "죄인으로 소문난 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 15:1-2; Readable says the man was known as a sinner, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: σταθεὶς δὲ Ζακχαῖος εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον· Ἰδοὺ τὰ ἡμίσιά μου τῶν ὑπαρχόντων, κύριε, τοῖς πτωχοῖς δίδωμι, καὶ εἴ τινός τι ἐσυκοφάντησα ἀποδίδωμι τετραπλοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Having stood then Zacchaeus said to the Lord, Look, the halves of me of the possessions, Lord, to the poor I give, and if of anyone anything I extorted I give back fourfold.

en.L: But Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Look, half of my possessions, Lord, I give to the poor; and if I have extorted anything from anyone, I give back four times as much."
en.B: But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Lord, see: half of what I own I am giving to the poor. And if I have taken anything from anyone by cheating, I am paying it back four times over."
en.R: Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord Jesus, "Lord, I will give half of everything I own to poor people. And if I have cheated anyone out of anything, I will pay that person back four times as much."

es.L: Pero Zaqueo, poniéndose en pie, dijo al Señor: «Mira, la mitad de mis bienes, Señor, la doy a los pobres; y si a alguien le he sacado algo con extorsión, le devuelvo cuatro veces más».
es.B: Pero Zaqueo se puso de pie y dijo al Señor: «Mira, Señor: la mitad de lo que tengo se la doy a los pobres. Y si he defraudado a alguien en algo, le devuelvo cuatro veces lo que le quité».
es.R: Zaqueo se puso de pie y le dijo al Señor Jesús: «Señor, daré a los pobres la mitad de todo lo que tengo. Y si le he quitado algo a alguien con engaños, le pagaré cuatro veces esa cantidad».

fr.L: Mais Zachée, se tenant debout, dit au Seigneur : « Voici, la moitié de mes biens, Seigneur, je la donne aux pauvres ; et si j’ai extorqué quelque chose à quelqu’un, je [lui] rends le quadruple. »
fr.B: Mais Zachée se leva et dit au Seigneur : « Seigneur, voici : je donne aux pauvres la moitié de ce que je possède. Et si j’ai pris quelque chose à quelqu’un en le trompant, je lui rends quatre fois plus. »
fr.R: Zachée s’est levé et il a dit au Seigneur Jésus : « Seigneur, je vais donner aux pauvres la moitié de tout ce que j’ai. Et si j’ai trompé quelqu’un pour lui prendre quelque chose, je vais lui rendre quatre fois plus. »

sw.L: Lakini Zakayo akasimama, akamwambia Bwana, "Tazama, nusu ya mali yangu, Bwana, nawapa maskini; na kama nimemdhulumu mtu yeyote kitu, namrudishia mara nne."
sw.B: Lakini Zakayo alisimama, akamwambia Bwana, "Bwana, tazama: nusu ya mali yangu ninawapa maskini. Na kama nimemdhulumu mtu yeyote kitu, ninamlipa mara nne."
sw.R: Zakayo alisimama, akamwambia Bwana Yesu, "Bwana, nitawapa maskini nusu ya mali yangu yote. Na kama nimemdanganya mtu yeyote nikachukua kitu chake, nitamlipa mara nne ya kiasi hicho."

vi.L: Nhưng Xa-chê đứng lên và nói với Chúa: "Lạy Chúa, kìa, phân nửa tài sản của con, con cho người nghèo; và nếu con đã tống tiền của ai điều gì, con trả lại gấp bốn."
vi.B: Nhưng Xa-chê đứng dậy thưa với Chúa: "Lạy Chúa, con xin đem một nửa tài sản của con cho người nghèo. Và nếu con đã gian lận lấy của ai điều gì, con xin hoàn trả gấp bốn lần."
vi.R: Xa-chê đứng dậy và nói với Chúa Giê-xu: "Lạy Chúa, con sẽ cho người nghèo một nửa tài sản của con. Và nếu con đã lừa gạt lấy của ai thứ gì, con sẽ trả lại cho người ấy gấp bốn lần."

ko.L: 그런데 삭개오가 서서 주님께 말했다. "보십시오, 제 재산의 절반을, 주님, 가난한 사람들에게 줍니다. 그리고 제가 누구에게서 무엇이든 부당하게 빼앗은 것이 있으면, 네 배로 갚습니다."
ko.B: 삭개오가 일어서서 주님께 말했다. "주님, 제가 가진 것의 절반을 가난한 사람들에게 주겠습니다. 그리고 제가 누구에게서 무엇이든 부당하게 빼앗은 것이 있으면, 네 배로 갚겠습니다."
ko.R: 삭개오가 일어서서 주 예수께 말했다. "주님, 제가 가진 모든 것의 절반을 가난한 사람들에게 주겠습니다. 그리고 제가 누구를 속여서 무엇이든 빼앗았다면, 그 사람에게 네 배로 갚아 주겠습니다."

pt.L: Mas Zaqueu, pondo-se de pé, disse ao Senhor: "Olha, Senhor, a metade dos meus bens eu dou aos pobres; e, se extorqui alguma coisa de alguém, devolvo quatro vezes mais."
pt.B: Mas Zaqueu se levantou e disse ao Senhor: "Senhor, olha: estou dando aos pobres a metade de tudo o que tenho. E, se tirei alguma coisa de alguém com fraude, estou devolvendo quatro vezes mais."
pt.R: Zaqueu se levantou e disse ao Senhor Jesus: "Senhor, eu vou dar aos pobres a metade de tudo o que tenho. E, se enganei alguém e tirei alguma coisa dele, vou devolver quatro vezes mais."

decisions.choice: I give, I give back: a promise Zacchaeus makes now, which takes effect at once
alternatives: a description of what he already does as his habit, defending himself against the grumbling
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the present tense. Some read them as his regular practice: he already gives half and repays any wrong. But Jesus answers that salvation has come today (19:9), and the story is about a sinner changed by meeting Jesus, so the present is best read as a decision he makes on the spot.

decisions.choice: extorted: got money from someone by threats or false charges
alternatives: made a mistake in the accounts
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John the Baptist used when he told soldiers not to extort money (3:14). "If" does not mean he doubts it; it means "whatever I have taken in this way".

decisions.choice: fourfold: the repayment the law required for a stolen sheep
decisions.reason: The law of Moses required a thief who killed or sold a stolen sheep to repay four sheep (Exodus 22:1; 2 Samuel 12:6). For ordinary wrongs, the law asked the full amount plus a fifth (Leviticus 6:5; Numbers 5:7). Zacchaeus takes on the heaviest penalty.

decisions.choice: the Lord; Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: Luke the narrator calls Jesus "the Lord" (7:13; 10:1; 18:6), and Zacchaeus addresses him with the same word.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, as at 12:42.

decisions.choice: I will give; I will pay
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the present tense as a promise (m1).

decisions.choice: le he sacado algo con extorsión (L); he defraudado (B); le he quitado algo con engaños (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is getting money from someone by threats or false charges (meaning decision m2), not plain theft, so none of the levels says "robar".

decisions.choice: kumdhulumu (L, B); kumdanganya mtu na kuchukua kitu chake (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is getting money from someone by threats or false charges (meaning decision m2). "Kudhulumu" is to wrong someone by taking what is theirs through force or abuse of position, closer than "kuiba" (steal).

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for the narrator's "the Lord" (L, B), "Chúa Giê-xu" (R); Zacchaeus says "Lạy Chúa" and "con"
decisions.reason: As in Luke 7:13 and 10:1. Zacchaeus now speaks as one who receives Jesus as Lord, so he uses the believer's address and calls himself "con" (style guide section 6).

decisions.choice: "con cho ... con trả lại" (L); "con xin" (B); "con sẽ" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek present is a promise that takes effect at once (meaning decision): Literal keeps the bare verbs, Balanced makes it a solemn pledge with "xin", Readable says it as a promise.

decisions.choice: "주님께" (L, B), "주 예수께" (R) for the narrator's "the Lord"; Zacchaeus speaks in 합쇼체 with "제"; "보십시오" (L) for idou in his speech, not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 7:13 and 12:42 for the narrator's title. Inside respectful speech the plain "보라" would be rude, so Literal uses the 합쇼체 form, as at Luke 15:29.

decisions.choice: "줍니다", "갚습니다" (L); "주겠습니다", "갚겠습니다" (B, R); "부당하게 빼앗다" (L, B), "속여서 빼앗다" (R) for sykophanteo
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present; Balanced and Readable make it a promise that takes effect now, as the meaning decision reads it. The verb means getting money by threats or false charges.

decisions.choice: Olha, Senhor (L); Senhor, olha (B)
decisions.reason: Zacchaeus speaks to Jesus, so the imperative is in the "tu" form, "olha" (style §4); "veja" would be the "você" form. "Eis" is kept for narration at Literal.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο, καθότι καὶ αὐτὸς υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: Said then to him the Jesus that Today salvation to the house this came, because also he a son of Abraham is;

en.L: And Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
en.B: Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this household. This man too is one of Abraham's sons.
en.R: Jesus said to him, "Today God has brought salvation to this house. This man belongs to God's people too. He is a true son of Abraham.

es.L: Y Jesús le dijo: «Hoy ha llegado la salvación a esta casa, porque también él es hijo de Abraham.
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Hoy ha llegado la salvación a esta familia. También este hombre es hijo de Abraham.
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Hoy Dios ha traído la salvación a esta casa. Este hombre también pertenece al pueblo de Dios. Es un verdadero hijo de Abraham.

fr.L: Et Jésus lui dit : « Aujourd’hui le salut est arrivé à cette maison, puisque lui aussi est un fils d’Abraham.
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Aujourd’hui, le salut est venu pour cette famille. Cet homme, lui aussi, est un des fils d’Abraham.
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Aujourd’hui, Dieu a apporté le salut dans cette maison. Cet homme fait partie, lui aussi, du peuple de Dieu. C’est un vrai fils d’Abraham.

sw.L: Naye Yesu akamwambia, "Leo wokovu umeifikia nyumba hii, kwa kuwa yeye pia ni mwana wa Ibrahimu.
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Leo wokovu umeifikia jamaa hii. Mtu huyu naye ni mmoja wa wana wa Ibrahimu.
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Leo Mungu ameleta wokovu katika nyumba hii. Mtu huyu naye ni mmoja wa watu wa Mungu. Yeye ni mwana halisi wa Ibrahimu.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Hôm nay sự cứu rỗi đã đến cho nhà này, vì người này cũng là con của Áp-ra-ham.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Hôm nay sự cứu rỗi đã đến với gia đình này, vì người này cũng là một con cháu của Áp-ra-ham.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Hôm nay Đức Chúa Trời đã đem sự cứu rỗi đến cho nhà này. Người này cũng thuộc về dân của Đức Chúa Trời. Ông là con cháu thật của Áp-ra-ham.

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "오늘 구원이 이 집에 이르렀다. 이 사람도 아브라함의 아들이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "오늘 구원이 이 집에 이르렀다. 이 사람도 아브라함의 자손이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 삭개오에게 말씀하셨다. "오늘 하나님께서 이 집에 구원을 주셨다. 이 사람도 하나님의 백성이다. 아브라함의 참 자손이다.

pt.L: E Jesus lhe disse: "Hoje a salvação veio a esta casa, porque também ele é filho de Abraão.
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "Hoje a salvação chegou a esta casa. Este homem também é um dos filhos de Abraão.
pt.R: Jesus disse a ele: "Hoje Deus trouxe a salvação para esta casa. Este homem também faz parte do povo de Deus. Ele é um verdadeiro filho de Abraão.

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue by God, here the forgiveness and new life that come with Jesus
decisions.reason: Zechariah praised God for salvation that comes through the forgiveness of sins (1:69, 77), and Simeon saw that salvation in the child Jesus (2:30). Salvation comes to Zacchaeus' house as Jesus enters it.

decisions.choice: this house: Zacchaeus and his household
decisions.reason: "House" often means the people who live in it (10:5; Acts 16:31).

decisions.choice: he too is a son of Abraham: a Jew, an heir of God's promise to Abraham, despite what people say of him
alternatives: he has become a son of Abraham by giving to the poor
decisions.reason: The crowd treat Zacchaeus as an outsider (19:7). Jesus says he belongs to God's people, to whom God promised mercy (1:54-55, 73). Jesus calls a crippled woman a daughter of Abraham in the same way (13:16).

decisions.choice: to him: to Zacchaeus, with the crowd listening
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to Zacchaeus but of him in the third person ("he too"), so the words are meant for those who grumbled as well.

decisions.choice: God has brought salvation; This man belongs to God's people too
alternatives: salvation has come; he too is a son of Abraham (alone)
decisions.reason: Readable says who brings salvation and what being a son of Abraham means (m3), and keeps the phrase itself.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 19:10
decisions.reason: The next sentence continues Jesus' words.

decisions.choice: "sự cứu rỗi" at every level
decisions.reason: The word used for salvation in Luke 1-3 (3:6), kept at every level.

decisions.choice: "구원" at every level; "아브라함의 아들" (L), "아브라함의 자손" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "구원" is the key term. "자손" is the Korean way to say a descendant and heir of Abraham, as at Luke 3:8 (R); one particular man is meant, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: esta casa
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "household". Portuguese "casa" means the people of a house as well as the building ("toda a casa dele"), so Balanced keeps the word of the Greek, which also takes up "a sua casa" of 19:5.

source.text: ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός.

records.literal_gloss: came for the Son of the Man to seek and to save the [thing] having been lost.

en.L: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
en.B: The Son of Man came to look for what was lost and to save it."
en.R: I, the Son of Man, came to look for people who are lost and to save them."

es.L: Porque el Hijo del Hombre vino a buscar y a salvar lo perdido».
es.B: El Hijo del Hombre vino a buscar lo que se había perdido y a salvarlo».
es.R: Yo, el Hijo del Hombre, vine a buscar a las personas que están perdidas y a salvarlas».

fr.L: Car le Fils de l’homme est venu chercher et sauver ce qui est perdu. »
fr.B: Le Fils de l’homme est venu chercher ce qui était perdu, pour le sauver. »
fr.R: Moi, le Fils de l’homme, je suis venu chercher les gens qui sont perdus, pour les sauver. »

sw.L: Kwa maana Mwana wa Adamu alikuja kutafuta na kuokoa kilichopotea."
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja kutafuta kilichopotea na kukiokoa."
sw.R: Mimi, Mwana wa Adamu, nilikuja kuwatafuta watu waliopotea na kuwaokoa."

vi.L: Vì Con Người đã đến để tìm và cứu những gì đã bị mất."
vi.B: Con Người đã đến để tìm kiếm và cứu những gì đã lạc mất."
vi.R: Ta là Con Người, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đến để tìm những người bị lạc mất và cứu họ."

ko.L: 인자가 잃어버린 것을 찾아 구원하러 왔기 때문이다."
ko.B: 인자는 잃어버린 것을 찾아서 구원하러 왔다."
ko.R: 나 인자, 곧 사람의 아들은 잃어버린 사람들을 찾아서 구원하려고 왔다."

pt.L: Pois o Filho do Homem veio procurar e salvar aquilo que se perdeu."
pt.B: O Filho do Homem veio procurar o que se tinha perdido e salvá-lo."
pt.R: Eu, o Filho do Homem, vim procurar as pessoas que estão perdidas e salvá-las."

decisions.choice: to seek and to save the lost: as God promised to seek his lost sheep
alternatives: a general saying with no background
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 34 God condemns Israel's shepherds, who did not seek the lost, and promises to seek the lost himself and bring them back (Ezekiel 34:4, 16). Jesus does what God said he would do. The parables of the lost sheep, coin and son make the same point (15:4-32).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
decisions.reason: As in 5:24 and 9:22. Here the title is joined to his mission to save.

decisions.choice: the lost: whatever is lost, here people who have strayed from God
decisions.reason: The form is singular and neuter, "that which has been lost", a general way of speaking of all who are lost, as in 15:4-6 and 15:24, 32.

decisions.choice: I, the Son of Man
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Jesus is speaking of himself (m2).

decisions.choice: what was lost (B); people who are lost (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the general sense of the neuter word; Readable says it is about people (m3). Literal has the familiar "the lost".

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre; "Yo" in Readable takes no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The title used through the Gospels (meaning decision m2). In Readable Jesus says "Yo, el Hijo del Hombre", as the English Readable says "I"; Jesus' "yo" takes no span, as the English "I" has none.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu; "Mimi" in Readable with no span
decisions.reason: The title used through the Gospels (meaning decision m2). In Readable "Mimi" opens the sentence and is capitalised either way, so it takes no deity_pronoun span, as the English "I" has none.

decisions.choice: "những gì đã bị mất" (L); "những gì đã lạc mất" (B); "những người bị lạc mất" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is neuter, "what is lost" (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep it, Readable names the people meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "인자" at every level, with "곧 사람의 아들" once (R) in this chapter; "왔다" with no honorific, as Jesus speaks of himself
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 5:24, 11:30 and 12:8.

source.text: Ἀκουόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ταῦτα προσθεὶς εἶπεν παραβολὴν διὰ τὸ ἐγγὺς εἶναι Ἰερουσαλὴμ αὐτὸν καὶ δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς ὅτι παραχρῆμα μέλλει ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναφαίνεσθαι·

records.literal_gloss: Hearing then of them these [things], having added he spoke a parable because of the near being Jerusalem him and the thinking them that immediately is about the kingdom of the God to appear;

en.L: While they were listening to these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went on to tell a parable, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear immediately.
en.B: As they listened to this, Jesus went on to tell them a parable. He did this because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was near Jerusalem, and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear at once.
en.R: The people were listening to all this. Then Jesus told them a story. He told it because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was getting close to Jerusalem. The people thought that God was going to set up his kingdom right away.

es.L: Mientras ellos oían estas cosas, prosiguió y dijo una parábola, por estar {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} cerca de Jerusalén y pensar ellos que el reino de Dios iba a manifestarse de inmediato.
es.B: Mientras escuchaban esto, Jesús les contó además una parábola. Lo hizo porque estaba cerca de Jerusalén y ellos pensaban que el reino de Dios iba a aparecer en seguida.
es.R: La gente estaba escuchando todo esto. Entonces Jesús les contó una historia. La contó porque ya estaba cerca de Jerusalén. La gente pensaba que Dios iba a empezar a reinar en ese mismo momento.

fr.L: Et comme ils écoutaient cela, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ajouta une parabole, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était près de Jérusalem et qu’ils croyaient que le royaume de Dieu allait apparaître sur-le-champ.
fr.B: Comme ils écoutaient ces paroles, Jésus leur raconta encore une parabole. Il le fit parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était près de Jérusalem et qu’ils s’imaginaient que le royaume de Dieu allait se manifester tout de suite.
fr.R: Les gens écoutaient tout cela. Alors Jésus leur a raconté une histoire. Il l’a racontée parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrivait près de Jérusalem. Les gens pensaient que Dieu allait établir {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume tout de suite.

sw.L: Basi walipokuwa wakisikia mambo haya, aliongeza akasema mfano, kwa sababu ya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa karibu na Yerusalemu, nao kudhani kwamba ufalme wa Mungu ulikuwa karibu kutokea mara moja.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakisikiliza maneno hayo, Yesu aliendelea, akawaambia mfano. Alifanya hivyo kwa sababu alikuwa karibu na Yerusalemu, nao walidhani kwamba ufalme wa Mungu ungetokea mara moja.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wakisikiliza mambo hayo yote. Kisha Yesu akawaambia mfano. Aliwaambia kwa sababu alikuwa anakaribia Yerusalemu. Watu walidhani kwamba Mungu angeanza kutawala mara moja.

vi.L: Và trong khi họ đang nghe những điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói thêm một ngụ ngôn, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở gần Giê-ru-sa-lem và họ nghĩ rằng vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời sắp hiện ra ngay lập tức.
vi.B: Trong khi họ đang nghe những lời ấy, Đức Giê-xu kể tiếp một ngụ ngôn. Ngài kể như vậy vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đến gần Giê-ru-sa-lem, và họ tưởng rằng vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời sắp xuất hiện ngay.
vi.R: Dân chúng đang lắng nghe tất cả những điều ấy. Rồi Đức Giê-xu kể cho họ một câu chuyện. Ngài kể câu chuyện ấy vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sắp đến Giê-ru-sa-lem. Dân chúng nghĩ rằng Đức Chúa Trời sắp lập vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngay lập tức.

ko.L: 그런데 그들이 이것들을 듣고 있을 때에, 그분이 덧붙여 비유 하나를 말씀하셨다. 그분이 예루살렘에 가까이 계셨고, 그들은 하나님의 나라가 곧 나타날 것이라고 생각하였기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사람들이 이 말씀을 듣고 있을 때에, 예수께서 비유 하나를 더 들려주셨다. 예수께서 예루살렘에 가까이 오셨고, 사람들은 하나님의 나라가 곧바로 나타날 것으로 생각하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사람들은 예수의 말씀을 듣고 있었다. 그때 예수께서 그들에게 비유 하나를 더 들려주셨다. 예수께서 예루살렘에 가까이 오셨기 때문이다. 사람들은 하나님께서 그분의 나라를 바로 세우실 것이라고 생각하고 있었다.

pt.L: E, enquanto eles ouviam essas coisas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} prosseguiu e contou uma parábola, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} estava perto de Jerusalém e eles pensavam que o Reino de Deus ia aparecer imediatamente.
pt.B: Enquanto eles ouviam isso, Jesus continuou e lhes contou uma parábola. Fez isso porque estava perto de Jerusalém, e eles supunham que o Reino de Deus ia se manifestar de imediato.
pt.R: As pessoas estavam ouvindo tudo isso. Então Jesus contou a elas uma história. Ele contou essa história porque estava chegando perto de Jerusalém. As pessoas pensavam que Deus ia começar a reinar ali mesmo, sem demora.

decisions.choice: having added: went on, adding a parable to what he had said
decisions.reason: The verb means to add. Jesus continues speaking to those who heard his words to Zacchaeus.

decisions.choice: the kingdom of God was going to appear immediately: they expected God's rule to be set up in Jerusalem at once
alternatives: they thought the kingdom was already present
decisions.reason: Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, the city of David. Many expected that the Messiah would take power there and drive out Israel's enemies (24:21; Acts 1:6). The parable tells of a king who goes away and comes back only after a long time.

decisions.choice: they: those who heard Jesus at Zacchaeus' house, including the grumblers
decisions.reason: The pronoun looks back to 19:7-10.

decisions.choice: two sentences: the parable, then the reasons
decisions.reason: The Greek gives the two reasons in one long clause. Balanced and Readable say first that he told a parable, then why.

decisions.choice: a story; God was going to set up his kingdom
alternatives: a parable; the kingdom of God was going to appear
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a parable is and what the people expected (m2).

decisions.choice: parábola (L, B); historia (R)
decisions.reason: As the English, which says "story" at Readable (decision r-en-2). The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: Dios iba a empezar a reinar
alternatives: Dios iba a establecer su reino
decisions.reason: Says what the English Readable says, that God would set up his rule at once (meaning decision m2), without a possessive pronoun the English leaves unmarked by the setting.

decisions.choice: une parabole (L, B); une histoire (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable says "a story" and as in Mark 12:1: what follows is a story, and "histoire" is the plain word for it.

decisions.choice: son royaume (R), with the deity_pronoun setting
alternatives: son royaume, with no span, as the English Readable "his kingdom"
decisions.reason: The possessive refers to God, and every pronoun for God carries the deity_pronoun setting; the English Readable has no span on "his" here.

decisions.choice: mfano at every level
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is the Swahili word for a parable and is plain enough for Readable too, where the English Readable says "story". The same through Luke.

decisions.choice: Mungu angeanza kutawala
decisions.reason: Says what the English Readable says, that God would set up his rule at once (meaning decision m2), without a possessive the English leaves unmarked by the setting.

decisions.choice: "ngụ ngôn" (L, B); "câu chuyện" (R) for parable
decisions.reason: As in Luke 8:4 and 13:6.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: The form used through Luke and Mark.

decisions.choice: "비유" at every level, Readable included; "곧" (L), "곧바로" (B), "바로" (R) for parachrema
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 8:4, 8:44 and 12:16.

decisions.choice: "하나님의 나라" (L, B); "하나님께서 그분의 나라를 ... 세우실" (R)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, which says that God would set up his rule.

decisions.choice: Deus ia começar a reinar
alternatives: Deus ia estabelecer o seu Reino
decisions.reason: Readable says what the people expected (m2) with a verb, which avoids a "seu" for God that the English Readable leaves without a deity_pronoun span.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν· Ἄνθρωπός τις εὐγενὴς ἐπορεύθη εἰς χώραν μακρὰν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ βασιλείαν καὶ ὑποστρέψαι.

records.literal_gloss: He said therefore, A man certain of noble birth went into a country distant to receive for himself a kingdom and to return.

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "A certain man of noble birth went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "A man from a noble family traveled to a faraway country to be made king there, and then to come back home.
en.R: Jesus said, "There was once a man from an important family. He went on a long journey to a country far away. He went there so that he could be made king, and then come back home.

es.L: Dijo, pues: «Cierto hombre de noble linaje se fue a un país lejano para recibir para sí un reino y volver.
es.B: Así que les dijo: «Un hombre de familia noble viajó a un país lejano para que allí lo hicieran rey, y luego volver a casa.
es.R: Jesús dijo: «Había una vez un hombre de una familia importante. Hizo un largo viaje a un país muy lejano. Fue allá para que lo nombraran rey y después volver a su casa.

fr.L: Il dit donc : « Un homme de noble naissance est parti pour un pays lointain, afin de recevoir pour lui la royauté et de revenir.
fr.B: Il dit donc : « Un homme d’une famille noble est parti pour un pays lointain, pour y être fait roi, puis revenir chez lui.
fr.R: Jésus a dit : « Il était une fois un homme d’une famille importante. Il est parti pour un long voyage, dans un pays très loin. Il y allait pour qu’on le fasse roi, et ensuite il voulait revenir chez lui.

sw.L: Basi akasema, "Mtu mmoja wa ukoo wa heshima alisafiri kwenda nchi ya mbali ili kujipatia ufalme na kurudi.
sw.B: Basi akasema, "Mtu mmoja wa jamaa ya heshima alisafiri kwenda nchi ya mbali ili afanywe mfalme huko, kisha arudi nyumbani.
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Palikuwa na mtu mmoja wa jamaa maarufu. Alisafiri safari ndefu kwenda nchi ya mbali. Alikwenda huko ili awekwe kuwa mfalme, kisha arudi nyumbani.

vi.L: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Có một người thuộc dòng dõi quý tộc đi đến một xứ xa để nhận vương quyền cho mình rồi trở về.
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Có một người thuộc dòng dõi quý tộc đi đến một xứ xa để được phong làm vua, rồi trở về.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói: "Ngày xưa có một người thuộc một gia đình quyền quý. Ông đi một chuyến xa đến một xứ ở rất xa. Ông đến đó để được phong làm vua, rồi sẽ trở về.

ko.L: 그래서 그분이 말씀하셨다. "귀족 출신의 어떤 사람이 자기를 위하여 왕권을 받아 가지고 돌아오려고 먼 나라로 갔다.
ko.B: 그래서 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "어떤 귀족이 왕위를 받아 오려고 먼 나라로 길을 떠났다. 왕이 되어 다시 돌아올 생각이었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "옛날에 훌륭한 집안의 한 사람이 있었다. 그는 아주 먼 나라로 긴 여행을 떠났다. 그 나라에 가서 왕으로 세움을 받고 다시 집으로 돌아오려는 것이었다.

pt.L: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Certo homem de família nobre foi para um país distante para receber para si um reino e voltar.
pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse: "Um homem de família nobre viajou para um país distante para ser feito rei ali e depois voltar para casa.
pt.R: Jesus disse: "Havia um homem de uma família importante. Ele fez uma longa viagem para um país muito distante. Foi até lá para ser feito rei e depois voltar para casa.

decisions.choice: went to a distant country to receive a kingdom: as the rulers of Judea went to Rome to be confirmed as kings
alternatives: he went to conquer a kingdom
decisions.reason: Rulers in the land of Israel held power only by the grant of Rome. When Herod the Great died in 4 BC, his son Archelaus went to Rome to ask the emperor to make him king, and a delegation of Jews followed him to argue against him. Jesus' hearers in Jericho, where Archelaus had built a palace, would know the story.

decisions.choice: a man of noble birth: in the story, a figure for Jesus, who goes away and will return as king
alternatives: only a story about a ruler of the day
decisions.reason: The parable answers the people's belief that the kingdom would appear at once (19:11). Like the nobleman, Jesus will go away and return later, and his servants must be faithful until then (12:35-48).

decisions.choice: kingdom: royal rule, the right to reign as king
decisions.reason: The word means kingship more than land. He returns having received it (19:15).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to the end of 19:27
alternatives: a new quotation for each part of the story
decisions.reason: The whole parable is Jesus' speech. What the people in it say is in single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: to be made king there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what receiving a kingdom means (m3).

decisions.choice: the parable of 19:12-27 in the passé composé at every level; the present "il lui dit" of 19:22 kept at Literal
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, as for the narration
decisions.reason: The parable is Jesus speaking, and the style guide keeps the tenses of speech for a story told inside a speech, as in Mark 4 and 12 and Luke 4:25; the passé simple would turn his words into written narrative. The imperfect and the plus-que-parfait are used as in any spoken story.

decisions.choice: recevoir pour lui la royauté (L); être fait roi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means royal rule, the right to reign (m3). "Recevoir un royaume" would suggest that he was given a territory in the far country; "la royauté" says the right to be king, which he then exercises at home (19:15).

decisions.choice: "vương quyền" (L); "được phong làm vua" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the right to reign (meaning decision), not a territory, so Literal says "royal power" rather than "vương quốc".

decisions.choice: "귀족 출신" (L), "귀족" (B), "훌륭한 집안" (R); "왕권" (L), "왕위" (B), "왕으로 세움을 받다" (R) for basileia
decisions.reason: Here basileia is the right to reign, not a territory (meaning decision), so Korean says "royal power" or "the throne" rather than "나라".

source.text: καλέσας δὲ δέκα δούλους ἑαυτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δέκα μνᾶς καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πραγματεύσασθε ἐν ᾧ ἔρχομαι.

records.literal_gloss: Having called then ten slaves of himself he gave to them ten minas and said to them, Do business while I come.

en.L: And calling ten of his slaves, he gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Do business until I come.'
en.B: Before he left, he called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas, one to each. 'Put this money to work until I come back,' he told them.
en.R: Before he left, he called ten of his servants. He gave each of them one mina. A mina was an amount of money worth about a hundred days' pay. He told them, 'Use this money to do business until I come back.'

es.L: Y llamando a diez esclavos suyos, les dio diez minas y les dijo: “{{plural_you:Negocien|Negociad}} mientras vengo”.
es.B: Antes de partir, llamó a diez de sus siervos y les dio diez minas, una a cada uno. “{{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} negocio con este dinero hasta que yo vuelva”, les dijo.
es.R: Antes de irse, llamó a diez de sus siervos. A cada uno le dio una mina. Una mina era una cantidad de dinero igual a lo que se ganaba en unos cien días de trabajo. Les dijo: “{{plural_you:Usen|Usad}} este dinero para hacer negocios hasta que yo vuelva”.

fr.L: Et, ayant appelé dix de ses esclaves, il leur a donné dix mines et leur a dit : “Faites des affaires jusqu’à ce que je vienne.”
fr.B: Avant de partir, il a appelé dix de ses serviteurs et leur a donné dix mines, une à chacun. “Faites fructifier cet argent jusqu’à mon retour”, leur a-t-il dit.
fr.R: Avant de partir, il a appelé dix de ses serviteurs. Il a donné à chacun d’eux une mine. Une mine était une somme d’argent qui valait environ cent jours de salaire. Il leur a dit : “Servez-vous de cet argent pour faire du commerce jusqu’à mon retour.”

sw.L: Basi akiisha kuwaita watumwa wake kumi, aliwapa mina kumi, akawaambia, 'Fanyeni biashara mpaka nitakapokuja.'
sw.B: Kabla ya kuondoka, aliwaita watumishi wake kumi, akawapa mina kumi, kila mmoja mina moja. Akawaambia, 'Zitumieni fedha hizi kufanya biashara mpaka nitakaporudi.'
sw.R: Kabla ya kuondoka, aliwaita watumishi wake kumi. Akampa kila mmoja wao mina moja. Mina moja ilikuwa kiasi cha fedha sawa na mshahara wa siku mia moja hivi. Akawaambia, 'Tumieni fedha hizi kufanya biashara mpaka nitakaporudi.'

vi.L: Và gọi mười nô lệ của mình đến, ông đưa cho họ mười mi-na và nói với họ: 'Hãy làm ăn cho đến khi ta đến.'
vi.B: Trước khi đi, ông gọi mười đầy tớ của mình đến và giao cho họ {{units:mười nén bạc|mười mi-na}}, mỗi người {{units:một nén|một mi-na}}. Ông dặn họ: 'Hãy dùng số tiền này mà làm ăn cho đến khi ta trở về.'
vi.R: Trước khi đi, ông gọi mười đầy tớ của mình đến. Ông giao cho mỗi người {{units:một nén bạc|một mi-na}}. {{units:Mỗi nén bạc|Mỗi mi-na}} bằng khoảng một trăm ngày công. Ông dặn họ: 'Hãy dùng số tiền này để buôn bán cho đến khi ta trở về.'

ko.L: 그리고 그는 자기 종 열 명을 불러 그들에게 열 므나를 주고 그들에게 말했다. '내가 올 동안 장사하여라.'
ko.B: 그는 떠나기 전에 자기 종 열 명을 불러서 한 사람에게 한 므나씩, 모두 열 므나를 주며 말했다. '내가 돌아올 때까지 이 돈으로 장사를 하여라.'
ko.R: 그는 떠나기 전에 자기 종 열 명을 불렀다. 그리고 그들에게 한 므나씩 나누어 주었다. 한 므나는 일꾼이 백 일 동안 일해야 받는 돈이었다. 그가 종들에게 말했다. '내가 돌아올 때까지 이 돈으로 장사를 하여라.'

pt.L: E, chamando dez dos seus escravos, ele lhes deu dez minas e lhes disse: 'Façam negócios até que eu venha.'
pt.B: Antes de partir, ele chamou dez dos seus servos e lhes deu dez minas, uma para cada um. 'Ponham este dinheiro para render até eu voltar', disse a eles.
pt.R: Antes de partir, ele chamou dez dos seus servos. Deu a cada um deles uma mina. Uma mina era uma quantia de dinheiro que valia mais ou menos cem dias de salário. Ele disse a eles: 'Usem este dinheiro para fazer negócios até eu voltar.'

decisions.choice: mina: a sum of money equal to a hundred drachmas, about a hundred days' wages
alternatives: a large fortune, like a talent
decisions.reason: A mina was a weight of silver, not a coin. It was worth a hundred drachmas, and a drachma, like a denarius, was a usual day's pay (15:8; 7:41). So each slave received a modest but real sum, about four months' wages. The parable of the talents in Matthew 25:14-30 speaks of far larger amounts.

decisions.choice: slaves: men owned by the nobleman, who managed his affairs
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for a slave. In large households trusted slaves often ran business for their master (12:42-43).

decisions.choice: ten slaves, ten minas: one mina each
decisions.reason: Each slave receives the same amount, and later each reports on "your mina" (19:16, 18, 20).

decisions.choice: do business while I come: trade with it until I return
decisions.reason: The verb means to trade or do business. The phrase that follows is an idiom for "while I am on my way", that is, until he comes.

decisions.choice: mina (every level)
decisions.reason: The amount is explained once, in Readable at 19:13 and in the meaning decision there. Repeating a modern sum each time the servants speak would make the dialogue hard to follow, so every level keeps the unit's own name. "Pound", the older rendering, now suggests British money.

decisions.choice: one to each (B); He gave each of them one mina (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what the story assumes (m3).

decisions.choice: A mina was an amount of money worth about a hundred days' pay
decisions.reason: Readable explains the amount once, in a sentence of its own, because the word mina is used again and again in the story (m1). A setting span here would leave the later uses unexplained.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R); their master is "señor", lowercase, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-4) and as in Matthew 25: the story is about faithful service, not slavery itself. The nobleman stands for Jesus (meaning decision m2), but he is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no setting. The same through 19:27.

decisions.choice: mina at every level; Readable explains its worth
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-1): a mina was a hundred days' wages (meaning decision m1), and the English keeps the word with no units setting, so Spanish does the same and Readable says what it was worth.

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as the English: Literal keeps that the men were owned (m2); Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", their role as the master's agents. This holds for the whole parable.

decisions.choice: une mine at every level
alternatives: a units setting with a modern sum
decisions.reason: As the English: the amount is explained once, in Readable here and in m1, and every level keeps the coin's name so that the dialogue stays easy to follow. In French "mine" also names a mine or a facial expression, but "dix mines", "ta mine a rapporté" leave no doubt here.

decisions.choice: mtumwa (L); mtumishi (B, R); their master is "bwana", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-4) and as in Matthew 25: the story is about faithful service, not slavery itself. The nobleman stands for Jesus (meaning decision m2), but he is a figure in a parable, so his pronouns take no setting. The same through 19:27.

decisions.choice: mina at every level; Readable explains its worth
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-1): a mina was a hundred days' wages (meaning decision m1), and the English keeps the word with no units setting, so Swahili does the same and Readable says what it was worth.

decisions.choice: {{units:mười nén bạc|mười mi-na}} (B, R), and the same through the parable; "mi-na" (L)
alternatives: mi-na at every level, as the English
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese money words follow Matthew 25:15 ("túi bạc" for the talent): Balanced and Readable say "nén bạc", a sum of silver Vietnamese readers know, with the Greek unit as the alternative, as the Vietnamese units setting does; Literal keeps "mi-na".

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos (whole parable)
decisions.reason: The style guide's rule for doulos, as in Mark 12:2 and Matthew 25:14.

decisions.choice: the nobleman says "ta" (lowercase, no span) and "ngươi" to his servants; they say "Thưa chủ", "chủ" and "tôi" (19:13-27)
decisions.reason: The forms of the master and servants in Matthew 25:14-30 and Luke 14:22-24; the king in the story is not addressed with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: "종" for doulos at every level, through 19:27; "므나" at every level, explained once (R)
decisions.reason: As the Korean Luke 12:37 and 14:16 for doulos. The coin keeps its name, as the English keeps "mina"; Readable gives its worth, as the English does, with no units span.

decisions.choice: The nobleman speaks to his servants in 해라체; they answer him in 합쇼체 and call him "주인님" (19:16-25)
decisions.reason: As masters and servants speak in the Korean Luke 13:7-8 and 14:21-22.

decisions.choice: mina (every level), with no units setting
decisions.reason: As in the English: the sum is explained once, in Readable here, and the word is kept each time the servants speak. Portuguese "mina" is also a mine, but "dez minas" given and earned leaves no doubt that it is money. "Libra", the word of older Portuguese versions, would suggest the British pound.

source.text: οἱ δὲ πολῖται αὐτοῦ ἐμίσουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρεσβείαν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Οὐ θέλομεν τοῦτον βασιλεῦσαι ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: But the citizens of him were hating him, and they sent a delegation after him saying, Not we want this one to reign over us.

en.L: But his citizens hated him, and they sent a delegation after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
en.B: But the people of his country hated him. They sent a delegation after him to say, 'We do not want this man to be our king.'
en.R: But the people of his own country hated him. So they sent some men after him with this message: 'We do not want this man to be our king!'

es.L: Pero sus ciudadanos lo odiaban, y enviaron una embajada tras él, diciendo: “No queremos que este reine sobre nosotros”.
es.B: Pero la gente de su país lo odiaba. Enviaron tras él una delegación para decir: “No queremos que este hombre sea nuestro rey”.
es.R: Pero la gente de su propio país lo odiaba. Así que mandaron a unos hombres detrás de él con este mensaje: “¡No queremos que este hombre sea nuestro rey!”.

fr.L: Mais ses concitoyens le haïssaient, et ils ont envoyé une délégation derrière lui pour dire : “Nous ne voulons pas que celui-ci règne sur nous.”
fr.B: Mais les gens de son pays le haïssaient. Ils ont envoyé derrière lui une délégation pour dire : “Nous ne voulons pas de cet homme pour roi.”
fr.R: Mais les gens de son propre pays le détestaient. Alors ils ont envoyé quelques hommes derrière lui avec ce message : “Nous ne voulons pas que cet homme soit notre roi !”

sw.L: Lakini raia wake walikuwa wakimchukia, wakatuma ujumbe nyuma yake, wakisema, 'Hatutaki huyu atawale juu yetu.'
sw.B: Lakini watu wa nchi yake walimchukia. Wakatuma wajumbe wamfuate waseme, 'Hatutaki mtu huyu awe mfalme wetu.'
sw.R: Lakini watu wa nchi yake mwenyewe walimchukia. Kwa hiyo walituma watu wamfuate na ujumbe huu: 'Hatumtaki mtu huyu awe mfalme wetu!'

vi.L: Nhưng dân của ông ghét ông, và sai một phái đoàn đi theo sau ông mà nói: 'Chúng tôi không muốn người này làm vua cai trị chúng tôi.'
vi.B: Nhưng dân trong xứ ghét ông. Họ sai một phái đoàn theo sau ông để nói: 'Chúng tôi không muốn người này làm vua của chúng tôi.'
vi.R: Nhưng dân trong xứ của ông ghét ông. Vì thế họ sai mấy người đi theo sau ông để nói: 'Chúng tôi không muốn người này làm vua của chúng tôi!'

ko.L: 그런데 그의 시민들은 그를 미워하고 있었다. 그래서 그들은 그의 뒤를 따라 사절단을 보내어 말했다. '우리는 이 사람이 우리 위에 왕이 되는 것을 원하지 않습니다.'
ko.B: 그러나 그 나라 백성은 그를 미워했다. 그래서 그의 뒤를 따라 사절단을 보내어 이렇게 말하게 했다. '우리는 이 사람이 우리의 왕이 되는 것을 원하지 않습니다.'
ko.R: 그러나 그 나라 사람들은 그를 미워했다. 그래서 그들은 몇 사람을 뒤따라 보내서 이렇게 말하게 했다. '우리는 이 사람이 우리 왕이 되는 것을 바라지 않습니다!'

pt.L: Mas os seus cidadãos o odiavam, e enviaram uma delegação atrás dele, dizendo: 'Não queremos que este [homem] reine sobre nós.'
pt.B: Mas o povo do seu país o odiava. Mandaram atrás dele uma delegação para dizer: 'Não queremos que este homem seja o nosso rei.'
pt.R: Mas o povo do próprio país dele o odiava. Por isso mandaram alguns homens atrás dele com esta mensagem: 'Não queremos este homem como nosso rei!'

decisions.choice: sent a delegation after him: to the ruler who would grant the kingdom, to argue against him
decisions.reason: So the Jews did when Archelaus went to Rome (19:12). The delegation follows him to the distant country.

decisions.choice: his citizens hated him: in the story, those of his own people who refuse Jesus as their king
decisions.reason: They are his own people. In Jerusalem the leaders will reject Jesus (19:39, 47; 20:14), and in 19:27 the king judges those who would not have him reign.

decisions.choice: were hating: their hatred went on
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a settled attitude.

decisions.choice: to be our king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a plain phrase for the verb "reign".

decisions.choice: The delegation's message in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: It is addressed to the ruler who grants the kingdom (meaning decision), a superior.

decisions.choice: "시민들" (L), "그 나라 백성" (B), "그 나라 사람들" (R); "사절단" (L, B), "몇 사람" (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose citizens they were in plain words.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπανελθεῖν αὐτὸν λαβόντα τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶπεν φωνηθῆναι αὐτῷ τοὺς δούλους τούτους οἷς δεδώκει τὸ ἀργύριον, ἵνα γνοῖ τί διεπραγματεύσαντο.

records.literal_gloss: And it came about in the returning him having received the kingdom, and he said to be called to him the slaves these to whom he had given the money, in order that he might know what they had gained by trading.

en.L: And it happened, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he gave orders for these slaves to whom he had given the money to be called to him, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
en.B: He was made king and came back home. Then he sent for the servants to whom he had given the money, to find out what profit each had made by his trading.
en.R: He was made king anyway, and he came back home. Then he sent for the servants he had given the money to. He wanted to know how much each of them had earned.

es.L: Y sucedió que, al regresar él después de recibir el reino, mandó que le llamaran a estos esclavos a quienes había dado el dinero, para saber qué habían ganado negociando.
es.B: Lo hicieron rey, y volvió a su tierra. Entonces mandó llamar a los siervos a quienes había dado el dinero, para saber cuánto había ganado cada uno con sus negocios.
es.R: De todos modos lo nombraron rey, y volvió a su casa. Entonces mandó llamar a los siervos a quienes les había dado el dinero. Quería saber cuánto había ganado cada uno.

fr.L: Et il est arrivé, quand il est revenu après avoir reçu la royauté, qu’il a fait appeler auprès de lui ces esclaves à qui il avait donné l’argent, afin de savoir ce qu’ils avaient gagné en faisant des affaires.
fr.B: Il a été fait roi et il est revenu chez lui. Alors il a fait appeler les serviteurs à qui il avait donné l’argent, pour savoir ce que chacun avait gagné en le faisant fructifier.
fr.R: Il a quand même été fait roi, et il est revenu chez lui. Alors il a fait venir les serviteurs à qui il avait donné l’argent. Il voulait savoir combien chacun d’eux avait gagné.

sw.L: Ikawa aliporudi akiisha kupokea ufalme, aliamuru watumwa hao aliokuwa amewapa fedha waitwe kwake, ili ajue walichopata kwa biashara.
